newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs fall sharply on BOJ deputy governor comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs fall sharply on BOJ deputy governor comments.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract fell sharply in late afternoon trade on Wednesday due to comments by the Bank of Japan's deputy governor on interest rates.

BOJ Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying on Wednesday that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it does not want to make a hasty decision.
The June stood at 123.69 at 0534 GMT, down sharply from previous day's close of 124.50.
The June earlier fell by more than one full point, to as low as 123.45.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield rose sharply after the comments and stood at 2.555 percent as of 0531 GMT.
The comment by the BOJ deputy governor caught the market off guard and triggered massive selling, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
